program: Free primary and behavioral health care
priceScope: Conditional full annual recipient recognized-resource cost per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents

what: Old Irving Park Community Clinic provides free primary and behavioral health care to uninsured adults in Chicago.
Volunteer clinicians and institutional partners support medication access, testing, counseling and specialist referrals.
The clinic offers continuity of care for people facing financial and practical access barriers.
strengths: Current medical and behavioral services establish an operating care mechanism.
Audits recognize much donated care and retain support costs.
Medication assistance and accessible care may protect health and household resources.
reservations: The undated patient panel is not a verified annual unique cohort.
Additional clinical response and actual otherwise-paid savings are unmeasured.
Volunteer capacity, alternative providers and marginal funding remain unresolved.

sections.what: Old Irving Park Community Clinic, EIN 33-1164946, is the whole recipient at 5425 W. Addison Street, Chicago. It offers primary and behavioral care, donated medications, medication assistance, testing and referrals through volunteers and partners. Current intake requires uninsured adults aged at least 18, Illinois residence, proof of income and income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level. It is appointment-based, not urgent care. The official donation page identifies the recipient and links its donation form; no transaction or fulfillment was tested.
sections.monitoring: The current page says more than 2,500 patients and over 150 volunteers, without a dated annual denominator. N=2,500 remains a rounded panel proxy and k=.5 a judged annual treated fraction, not an observed 1,250 annual cohort. One patient per distinct household is another explicit judgment, not verified household deduplication. Request annual unique patients, residence, completed treatments, symptoms/function, actual spending and alternative care. Historical visit counts and the $6 retail-service claim per donated dollar do not establish current health or cash productivity. The FY 2024 cost and current undated panel are unmatched in period.
sections.qualitative: The randomized Oregon Medicaid experiment supports access and financial-protection mechanisms but found no significant changes in measured blood pressure, cholesterol or glycated hemoglobin over two years. Depression and financial strain improved. Insurance coverage is not this clinic's care package; those results do not calibrate OIPCC's response fraction, utility, avoided medical spending or mortality. The retained alpha .30 incremental responder share, .05 utility and half-year relief are explicitly unsupported local priors, not an empirically calibrated expected value. Behavioral and physical symptom relief form one bounded clinical area; referrals, prescriptions and mortality are not stacked. Current Illinois HBIA coverage for adults ended June 2025, but Cook County CareLink and other clinics remain alternatives. Need is not proof of full clinic attribution.
sections.cost:
Original FY 2024 audited whole-clinic expense is $1,060,786, including management and fundraising. Its $660,816 nonfinancial contribution is already matched by expense, not an addback. Note 3 says $660,815 and retains a mislabeled 2023 heading: a $1 discrepancy and drafting error, not silently corrected. The note excludes volunteer services failing recognition criteria. FY 2023 and FY 2022 audited expenses are $1,181,581 and $1,436,262; comparable recognized accrual mean $1,226,209.67. The latest current financial index lists 2024, not a verified 2025 audit. Recognized fair value is not demonstrated economic opportunity cost. Central factor 1 retains the recognized value as a conditional resource-cost reference; .5/1.5 donor-resource valuation and $50,000 extra unrecognized recipient-resource stresses are explicit judgments. They are not next-dollar cash budgets. Depreciation is retained; capital assets are not all recurring marginal expenses.

The full annual denominator is paired with 2,500 panel proxy × .5 annual activity × .4 additional annual funded-work response =500 exposed households. Clinical .30 additional responders gives 150 residents within that union; .05 utility × .5 year after a quarter-year delay at 3% gives 3.647943 Chicago clinical QALYs with judged residence share .98. b=.4 is the conditional fraction of annual work additional after replacement funding and binding capacity, not a second donor haircut on observed incremental outcomes. b=1 is separately shown. The ordinary gift response is unpriced.

A separate .30 resource-success hypothesis gives 150 households $300 of medical spending they would actually otherwise pay within one year, net of insurance/assistance, forgone care, replacement and taxes/benefits. It is not a $300 retail care value or an inference that all uninsured people buy treatment. Each positive component retains .5 for health overlap, then full $100 incremental time, travel, childcare and additional care burden versus alternative care is subtracted. These 150 households gain $50;350 other exposed households lose $100. Resource responders need not be clinical responders; overlap is handled at the positive resource component. One welfare-equivalent person per household, $20,000 annual resources and one joint log give −.671152 equivalents after residence and delay. Extra family welfare is unpriced. Central workGain 0 is unknown-neutral, not measured zero; a positive net-work hypothesis models nonfatal missed paid work avoided after taxes, benefit withdrawal and new costs, not ordinary survivor wages.

Clinical plus resource 2.976791 implies $3.563522 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents, not ten clinical QALYs. The initial $2.886493 million health-only price is preserved. The increase reflects finite delay and explicit signed household burdens, not new demonstrated efficacy or forced favorable change. Clinical-null retains resource exposure and all costs; zero savings, full unknown, adverse and zero expansion are distinct controls. Full union clinical harm is not shrunk by resource success. Positive-only overlap never attenuates negative resource components. Payer/provider margin loss, outside care costs and unrecognized recipient costs are separate stresses. Central outside incidence is unknown-neutral and incomplete, not complete world benefit; nonlocal household resources and public opportunity costs remain unpriced.
sections.funding: FY 2024 audit revenue is $1,304,302, government grant $263,484 and net assets $1,107,740. The current donation-form statement of no government funding and older audited grant receipts concern different periods and need reconciliation; they do not establish current falsehood or misconduct. Note 3's matching donated expense shows why cash cost alone cannot rank economic efficiency. Institutional referrals and donated capacity are constraints, not costless infinite expansion. CareLink offers eligible uninsured Cook County residents discounted care at county facilities regardless of immigration status, with application and renewal requirements; its former presumptive HBIA eligibility window ended June 2026 and is not assumed currently automatic. Prescriptions and transport have separate limitations. Other free/sliding-fee clinics, insurance eligibility and medication assistance continue in the counterfactual. No priced unfunded expansion, staff bottleneck or funding replacement rate was verified. Complete annual portfolio and marginal donor EV remain unknown.

model.geographicAttribution: Patient g=.98 judged MSA residence applies to health and resources; local counterparty stress g=1. Nonlocal resources unpriced.
model.formula: annual=N*k; exposed=annual*b; clinical=exposed*a; Q_all=clinical*u*discounted(T)−exposed*harm/discount(delay); Q_MSA=Q_all*g. Separate resourceSuccess partitions households; positive-only signed medical/work components jointly net full costs before .5*persons*discounted years*log(1+net/baseline). Effective C=C−donatedUSD+factor*donatedUSD+unrecognizedCostUSD. Price10=10*effective C/(clinical+resource equivalents).
model.counterfactual: Cook County CareLink, insurance eligibility, other clinics, medication assistance and partner capacity continue; some patients otherwise forgo rather than buy care.
model.attribution: Annual activity, incremental annual capacity, clinical response, resource success and residence are distinct judgments, not independent measured probabilities. Clinical/resource responder equality is not assumed.
model.uncertainty: Conditional reference, not calibrated expected value. Unmatched panel/year, causal utility, actual spending and marginal donation response unresolved.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional completed symptom-relieving care, finite morbidity utility and signed actual otherwise-paid medical spending/work resources; no retail care value or survivor wages.

historicalAlphaModel.counterfactual: a is the share with meaningful morbidity relief beyond equivalent alternative care; b separately discounts replacement funding and constrained volunteer capacity. No mortality benefit is credited.
historicalAlphaModel.attribution: One morbidity pathway only. Other health pathways are provisionally assigned zero net benefit, not demonstrated zero or a lower bound. Visits, prescriptions and retail care values are not added as QALYs. Cross-recipient benefits cannot be summed without person-level deduplication.
historicalAlphaModel.uncertainty: All utility, causal response, duration, funding additionality and residence parameters are illustrative judgments, not measured causal effects, calibrated expected values, confidence intervals or marginal gift purchase prices. Different accounting treatment of donated care prevents comparative economic-efficiency rankings.
sensitivity: Poor and favorable scenarios vary several uncalibrated assumptions together; they are not exhaustive bounds.
Zero additionality produces zero QALYs and no finite price.
Changing cost alone scales price proportionally; changing any multiplicative benefit factor inversely scales price.
At otherwise central assumptions, k=.25/.5/1 yields half/base/double benefit. Current panel and FY2024 expenses are unmatched in time.
missingInputs: Recipient causal morbidity and health-utility outcomes with follow-up and alternative-care comparison.
Additional unrestricted dollars, priced unfunded expansion and binding staff/volunteer constraints.
Patient residence, overlap across services and clinics, and incremental economic cost of donated resources.
Dated annual unique-patient count and matched cost/activity year.
historicalAlphaModel.costScope: Full FY2024 audited recipient expense, including recognized nonfinancial resources and support costs. Unrecognized volunteer time and external partner costs remain outside accounting expense; accounting value is not opportunity cost.
historicalAlphaModel.geographicAttribution: Clinic at 5425 W Addison Street, Chicago, anchors service in Cook County within the pinned 13-county Chicago MSA. g=.98 is judged residence share, not measured; Kenosha is excluded.
historicalAlphaModel.nativeOutcomes: Current panel exceeds 2,500, but an annual denominator was not established; annual activity is modeled with k, not asserted observed.
